REV-1 [R2] Resource-fetching string forms get through the value filter. Only matters if style values ever come from untrusted input. Consider also rejecting image-set( and src( .
REV-2 [PERF-001] Check styleElement.isConnected before reuse and re-append when it is detached.
REV-3 [PERF-001] Documentation should recommend a stable (module-level or memoised) style object for large lists.
REV-4 [UI-001] Configured looks are missing before hydration, so a toggle may briefly show the built-in look. This is a known trade-off of the design. Mention it in the docs.
REV-5 [R9] Unrelated whitespace change on an existing line; the repo policy asks for minimal diffs. No behaviour change.
REV-6 [R8] Collision is very unlikely, but a longer hash or a body-keyed registry would remove the risk.

QA-1 [R7] Stronger proof would be a test that the built-in toggle focus class or rule is present for on and off. The pre-existing toggle tests and the no-override assertion cover the main risk, so this is not blocking.
QA-2 [R8] Add a console.error/console.warn spy to one ignored-setting test. Behaviour is otherwise covered (null returned, button stays mounted).
QA-3 [R9] Consider an SSR test (renderToString with a styled provider, no document access during render) and a note that React 19 is covered only by the peer-dependency range. Advisory.
QA-4 [R3] Ordering is a reasonable proxy and the integration test keeps the pressed state on a disabled toggle, so this is not blocking.

QA-5 [R2] Not provable in this project's setup, so it is recorded as advisory. Run a one-off gzip size comparison of dist before release. Also not run: the packed-library install and import under CommonJS and ES modules (no scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs).

SEC-1 [USR-003] A value can still make the browser request an external URL (tracking beacon) without writing url(). This does not add rules or scripts, so R-security (single property only) holds; the values come from the app developer, not end users. Consider also rejecting image-set(, image(, src(, cross-fade(, element( or documenting that values are trusted.

SEC-2 [USR-003] Unbounded input is a low-severity DoS/memory risk if a very large or dynamically generated style object is supplied. Consider a cap on properties per state, or document that the config must be static.

SEC-3 [USR-003] Two different style bodies that collide would share the first one's CSS. This is a correctness risk rather than a vulnerability; accidental collision is unlikely and an attacker would already control the developer config. Consider keying the registry by the full css string, or comparing css on reuse.

SEC-4 [USR-003] Under a strict CSP (style-src without 'unsafe-inline') the injected rules are blocked and toggles fall back to the library defaults. The library already injects CSS at runtime (rollup inject: true), so this is consistent with the existing behaviour. Worth a documentation note.

SEC-5 [USR-003] Each render of such a button recompiles its style and adds a throwaway cache entry (garbage-collected via WeakMap). The work is bounded by one button's style and does not leak, so this is only a note; the docs should recommend hoisting style objects.
